_source: Which sentences of ADR-137 and of the khive-wire-protocol crate documentation each Amendment 1 decision displaces. The derived passages of the amendment's 'Precedence over the crate documentation' and 'Implementation fences' sections are generated from this table by scripts/lint-adr-137-displacements.py, which also cross-checks every decision's label against the ADR's own heading text. Rows are established by reading the cited sources directly; a field name is not a reliable key for this work, the call site is.
_row6_note: Decision 6 is recorded against the amendment text as it now stands, in which the decision requires the sequence and direction rules on BOTH endpoint roles. An earlier draft of the decision covered the server role only, and under that reading the crate documentation displaced nothing, because the crate already documents a server-side gate. Under the current reading the two statements that scope the gate to the server are exactly what is displaced. The row is stated here so that a reader can see the crate documentation changed status because the decision widened, not because the crate changed.

parent_displaced.quote: a server supports the current version and at least the immediately prior version

crate_displaced.quote: A server supports the current version and at least the immediately prior version.
crate_displaced.gloss: the versioning section restates the parent's compatibility rule in its unbounded form

parent_displaced.quote: the exact numeric defaults for frame-size ... limits
the numeric limit defaults remain implementation-phase deliverables

crate_displaced.quote: Explicit `null` on an optional field is equivalent to absence ... Duplicate members are last-wins, not rejected.
crate_displaced.gloss: the module documentation's stated boundaries on optional-null equivalence and duplicate members

decisions.label: CHANGED
decisions.subject: Unknown error codes

crate_displaced.quote: an unrecognized code falls back to `internal`, request-terminal
unknown codes fall back rather than decode-failing and are treated as `internal` despite unknown scope
crate_displaced.gloss: the wire-error module's own documentation, which quotes the parent's superseded sentence verbatim and presents it as the governing rule

decisions.scope_note: for the id-less case only, per that decision's own split

decisions.label: CHANGED
decisions.subject: Handshake sequence violations

crate_displaced.quote: implements the server side of this sequence as a type
crate_displaced.gloss: the handshake gate's documentation, which presents a server-side-only gate as the implementation of the sequence rule
the handshake module's own scope statement

decisions.scope_note: the rule is unaltered; what is displaced is its scoping to one endpoint role

crate_displaced.gloss: the module documentation's opaque-payload-fidelity section, together with the named codec test it cites as pinning that behaviour

decisions.label: CHANGED
decisions.subject: `event.payload` must be a JSON object

crate_displaced.gloss: the characterization of `event.payload` as data whose shape the crate does not own, as it applies to the outermost type only

decisions.scope_note: the per-field shape of a topic's payload remains the catalog's business; only the outermost type is displaced
